issues: Carry-over React hydration warning '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' from devtools instrumentation in PeriodSelector. Cosmetic console noise only, same as iteration_5/6.

critical_code_review_comments: /public/customer-login-code iterates ALL customers linearly (async for row in db.customers.find(...)) matching last 8 digits of phone in Python. On a 300-row demo this is fine but will degrade at scale. Suggest normalizing & indexing a phone_digits_last8 field on write, or at least adding an index on 'phone' and switching to a regex query ending with tail.

No rate limiting on /public/customer-login-code — only 10^6 code space, so a bot could brute-force a customer's 6-digit code in minutes. Recommend: lock the customer (or IP) after N failed attempts within a window; same pattern already discussed for kiosk PIN.

/storefront/sections endpoints trust client-supplied id strings; two sections with the same id would silently de-dup in the UI drag-drop reorder. Add server-side uniqueness check (set(len(ids)) == len(sections)) before upsert.

StorefrontSectionsIn.sections has no per-item schema (likely Dict[str, Any]). Any shape is accepted, which means a malformed row from an older client could crash Home.jsx at render time. Consider a Pydantic discriminated union per section type.

Account.jsx stores the raw JWT in sessionStorage (KEY='dina_customer') — fine for session resumption, but defeats the httpOnly cookie's XSS protection, since a stored XSS payload could exfiltrate the token. Prefer relying on the cookie alone and dropping token from storage.

In Account.jsx loadMe effect [L28-30] uses an empty dep array but reads session?.token — ok for mount, but if the component later receives a new session via setSession, loadMe won't re-run (works today because onDone also calls loadMe explicitly). Minor foot-gun.

gen_access_code() uses random.randint — not cryptographically random. For a 6-digit customer secret this should be secrets.randbelow(1_000_000) to avoid predictability. Low risk on current prod threat model but trivial to fix.
